title: simple-dispatcher: one way to read an on/off setting from the environment
description:
Repo: **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher**.

## Why

Each on/off setting in `config.js` parses its environment variable its own way, and default-on and default-off flags parse differently. LIN-4127 (making the usage relay default on) had to stop and decide what counts as "off", and whether an empty or garbage value means on or off, because of that. Its builder: with one helper, the ticket "would have been a one-word default change". LIN-4165 hit the same thing a few hours earlier.

## What we want

How an on/off setting is read from the environment is decided once, and every flag uses it, so making a flag default-on or default-off is a one-word change. The copies are deleted in the same change. Today's behaviour for values people actually set (`1`, `0`, `true`, `false` and so on) stays the same, and any change for odd values is named.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

A Survey looked at the ground first. Its advice, which we're taking:

* **First, a table-driven test that records today's behaviour at every site** (the Survey counted 16 parsers, some outside `config.js`): `1/0/true/false/yes/no/on/off` in mixed case and padded, plus empty, spaces, garbage and unset. Then swap the sites over one at a time and keep the table green. The Survey's reading is that both idioms already follow one rule, where only the word for the opposite of the default changes anything. If so, nothing changes behaviour, and the PR can say so. **Avoid a "smarter" helper:** it would change what garbage means for a default-on flag.
* **Put the helper in a leaf module with no dependencies.** Some modules deliberately don't load `config.js`, because loading it reads `.env` as a side effect, and that would be an unnamed behaviour change. It should also parse a raw value, for the callers that take one as a parameter.
* `SD_REAP_LEFTOVER_CLAUDE` (`off` or `log`) isn't an on/off flag, so leave it out and say so. Update the "same idiom … copied verbatim" comments in the same change.

## Implementation Plan

*(Pruned at close-out; the full plan is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.)*

**Implemented as approved.** PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/310](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/310>) (merged as `2f7b943`) added the leaf module `env-flag.js` (`parseFlag`, `envFlag`), swapped all 16 on/off sites over to it, deleted the copies, added the characterization table (`test/env-flag-sites.test.js`), the helper test and the no-duplicates/leaf guard, and updated the stale "copied verbatim" comments and `docs/module-map.md` (census 44). No behaviour change for any input. `SD_REAP_LEFTOVER_CLAUDE` and the integer knobs were left out deliberately. The only deviation: four `watch-restart*` tests now copy `env-flag.js` into their fake checkouts, because `instance-guard.js` requires it.

Scope and session fit: **fits one session**.

plan-review due: no

comments.body:
PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/310 (branch feat/lin-4182-env-flag-helper, commit 85c19a1)

**What changed:** new leaf module `env-flag.js` with `parseFlag(raw, defaultOn)` and `envFlag(name, defaultOn, env)`. All 16 on/off sites now use it (8 default-on + 3 default-off in config.js, plus oplog.js, resource-metrics.js, and instance-guard.js's isTruthy). The copies are deleted in the same change. Comments that called them "copied verbatim" now point at env-flag.js.

**Behaviour:** no change for any input. The characterization table (test/env-flag-sites.test.js) covers 1/0/true/false/yes/no/on/off, mixed case, padded, empty, whitespace, garbage and unset across all 16 sites. It was written and green on the old code before the swap, and stays green with no edits. `SD_REAP_LEFTOVER_CLAUDE` stays out (not an on/off flag).

**Evidence:**
- CI (unit tests, Ubuntu, Node 22): SUCCESS on the PR head.
- `npm test`: 3887 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (baseline 3854 pass).
- Guard test fails on the pre-change code (16 copies found); passes after.
- `npm run test:system`: 4 failing tests with the same names on untouched main against the same Harbour checkout, so pre-existing and not from this PR.
- `npm run test:mutation`: not run (needs HARBOUR_DIR and edits Harbour's source).

Merge is not mine: it waits for review.

## Review — LIN-4182

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/310 at head `85c19a1c07ed2f7d2def915d5f651b033929cb04` (base `main` @ `11a1279`).

CI: green. The `unit tests` check (CI workflow, `npm ci && npm test`) passed on head 85c19a1: 3871 pass, 0 fail. The log shows the new env-flag guard and leaf tests ran.

### Scope vs plan
The diff matches the plan's places exactly: `env-flag.js` (new), `config.js` (13 sites), `oplog.js`, `resource-metrics.js`, `instance-guard.js` (`isTruthy` deleted), `docs/module-map.md` (new bullet, census bumped 43 → 44), three new tests, and four `watch-restart*` tests that now copy `env-flag.js` into their fake checkout, since `instance-guard.js` requires it. That last change is a direct consequence of the leaf import, not an overrun. `SD_REAP_LEFTOVER_CLAUDE` and the integer knobs are untouched, as planned.

### Regression check
`git log -- config.js oplog.js resource-metrics.js instance-guard.js` shows LIN-4181, LIN-4127, LIN-4172, LIN-4165, LIN-4077 and LIN-796. Each polarity they set is preserved: WORKER_USAGE_RELAY and ASSISTANT_TEXT_RELAY are still default-on (LIN-4127/4165), `instance-guard.js` stays free of config.js (LIN-796), and the STATE_DIR imports are intact (LIN-4077). No revert is re-applied.

### Behaviour, independently re-run
- I ran the characterization table (`test/env-flag-sites.test.js`) **on main's old code**: 19/19 pass. On the PR head the three new test files pass 33/33. So the claim that the table was "green before and after with no edits" holds.
- The guard on main's old code lists exactly the plan's 16 sites: config.js 398, 484, 831, 856, 1279, 1311, 1324, 1335, 1343, 1359, 1373, 1385, 1394; instance-guard.js:130; oplog.js:33; resource-metrics.js:40.
- Raw non-string params: the old `String(v || '')` and the new `parseFlag(v, false)` agree for every falsy value (`0`, `false`, `''`, `null`, `undefined`). Both are off for default-off sites, so there is no hidden change.
- Standalone path: at the PR head, `node instance-guard.js --check <pidfile>` behaves the same as on main (exit 1 for a dead pid). Loading it pulls only `instance-guard.js` and `env-flag.js` into `require.cache`, so `.env` is not loaded.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| M1: "smarter" helper, so garbage gives off for default-on flags | sites + helper tests **6 fail** ✅ |
| M2: `require('./config')` appended to env-flag.js | guard **2 fail** (source-scan and require.cache) ✅ |
| M3: inline copy put back in oplog.js | guard **1 fail** ✅ |
| M4: `envFlag('SD_RESOURCE_RELAY', true)` (wrong default at one site) | sites table **6 fail** ✅ |

All load-bearing tests go red for the reason they name.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "an on/off env setting parsed inline". The plan's regex sweep plus my own sweep found no other instance:
- No `process.env.X === '1'/'true'`, `!== '0'`, `!!process.env` or `Boolean(process.env…)` in non-test JS.
- No shell-side `SD_*` boolean comparisons in `*.sh`, `scripts/` or `deploy/`.
- The only hit outside the 16 sites is `experiments/chrome-extension` (a DOM attribute, not env).

All 16 instances are handled, so the class is closed.

### Test level
Pure parser → unit tests (`env-flag.test.js`). Real-module behaviour → the per-input child-process table loads the real config.js, oplog.js, resource-metrics.js and instance-guard.js with load-env stubbed, and it asserts that the empty and unset rows were really seen. That level is right for this change.

### Checklist
Tests cover the change ✅ · state is clean (child processes, nothing written) ✅ · shared-path interactions: one input is set on all flags at once ✅ · security: no new surface ✅ · error handling: unchanged ✅ · style matches the codebase ✅ · performance: one-time load parse, no change ✅

### Fix for close-out (comment wording only, no behaviour change)
- `config.js` ~line 829–830 (LAUNCH_BREAKER_ENABLED block). The rewrite left a broken sentence: "…instead of accidentally defeating the breaker. Same boolean idiom as / read through envFlag (env-flag.js), default ON: 0/false/no/off disables."
  - Replace `Same boolean idiom as\n// read through envFlag (env-flag.js), default ON: 0/false/no/off disables.` with `Read through envFlag\n// (env-flag.js), default ON: 0/false/no/off disables.`
  - The guard is unaffected: the line contains `0/false/no/off`, not the `|`-joined marker.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **`npm run test:mutation` was not run by the author** (needs HARBOUR_DIR). *Inside* the plan's witness list. **Discharged** by static check: the only mutation entry anchored in a touched file (`config.js`, `fastFailBackoffWarning` find-string) still occurs exactly once at 85c19a1. No entry targets oplog.js, resource-metrics.js, instance-guard.js or env-flag.js, so no anchor this PR could have broken.
- **Standalone `watch-restart.sh` → `node instance-guard.js --check` path**, a user-reachable entry that `npm test` drives only through fake checkouts. *Inside* (the leaf-module constraint). **Discharged**: I ran it at the PR head; it matches main and loads only instance-guard.js and env-flag.js.
- **`npm run test:system`: 4 failures that the author reports fail identically on untouched main.** *Outside*: these tests do not exercise flag parsing differently from the unit table, and nothing in this deliverable depends on them. I did not re-run them (they need a Harbour checkout). Close-out should check whether a ticket already tracks these 4 failures and file one only if none exists.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The refactor is complete and behaviour-preserving, verified on both old and new code and by mutation. The one remaining item is the one-line comment fix in config.js named above, plus the outside-scope test:system follow-up check.

## Close-out — LIN-4182

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/310, squash-merged as `2f7b94325b9c23dfc81cfd015d0c016c13d48a7c`, pinned with `--match-head-commit c87f26b`. Review verdict was Approve, conditional on this close-out discharging the ledger.

**Change I made (the only one):** `c87f26b` fixes the broken comment sentence above `LAUNCH_BREAKER_ENABLED` in `config.js`. It now reads "Read through envFlag (env-flag.js), default ON: 0/false/no/off disables." This answers review's "Fix for close-out" item. It is comment-only, with no behaviour change and no new design.

**CI:** this repo has CI (`.github/workflows`, the `unit tests` check). I re-read the rollup on the new head `c87f26b` after the push: `unit tests` SUCCESS. Merge was pinned to that commit. CI is citeable but not enforceable on this repo, so I read the check rather than relying on a block. On merged main (`2f7b943`) I also ran `npm test` locally: 3892 tests, 3887 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

**Ledger:**
- `npm run test:mutation` not run by the author (inside): discharged by review's static check. The only mutation anchor in a touched file (`config.js`, the `fastFailBackoffWarning` find-string) still occurs once, and no entry targets `oplog.js`, `resource-metrics.js`, `instance-guard.js` or `env-flag.js`. My comment edit is outside that anchor. I did not run the mutation suite: it edits the Harbour checkout and needs `HARBOUR_DIR`. An open ruling row (`lin4182-run-mutation`, recommended "skip") already covers that question, so I did not raise it again.
- Standalone `watch-restart.sh` → `node instance-guard.js --check` (inside): discharged by review, who ran it at the PR head. It matches main and loads only `instance-guard.js` and `env-flag.js`. The leaf test in `npm test` keeps guarding it.
- 4 `npm run test:system` failures on untouched main (outside): already tracked, so nothing new filed. They are LIN-4185 (halt-mechanism), LIN-4186 (harbour-halt), LIN-4187 (observation-feed) and LIN-4188 (tap1-openrouter), each stating it fails identically on clean main. I linked all four as `related` to this ticket.

**Post-deploy:** the ledger has no post-deploy step. This is a behaviour-preserving refactor with no data clean-up or migration. I checked the landed code by running `npm test` on merged main as above, including the characterization table and guard/leaf tests. I have not confirmed that the host deploy follower has picked up `2f7b943`; there is no step that depends on it.

**Housekeeping:** I took a description snapshot before pruning and confirmed it carries the full pre-prune description. The "Implementation Plan" section is now a stub that records the PR, that the plan was implemented as approved, and the one deviation (the four `watch-restart*` tests copy `env-flag.js`). Problem statement and approach are kept.

**Not run:** `npm run test:mutation` (needs `HARBOUR_DIR`; discharged statically as above) and `npm run test:system` (needs a Harbour checkout; failures are tracked in LIN-4185 to LIN-4188).

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** It mostly wasn't. The plan had already done the hard part: it established that both idioms follow one rule, so the helper could be dumb. The change pushed against three things:
- Config constants are read at module load, and `load-env.js` refills any falsy key from `.env`. So the characterization table needed one child process per input, with `load-env` stubbed and the child reporting what it actually saw.
- The real binding was `instance-guard.js`. It had zero sibling requires, and four `watch-restart*.test.js` fixtures depend on that by copying it alone into a fake checkout. Adding `require('./env-flag')` broke `--check` there. I found it from a full-suite failure, not from reading.
- My own tooling. A scripted multi-file edit replaced a fixture line instead of adding beside it. I caught it in `git diff --stat`, but only because the line count looked wrong.

**2. What would I have done first?** I would grep for tests that copy root modules one file at a time before adding any require. I would also run `test:system` on untouched main up front. Its 4 failures are pre-existing, and knowing that early would have saved a second full run and a baseline worktree.

**3. What would I tidy?**
- The four watch-restart fixtures each hand-copy `instance-guard.js`, and now `env-flag.js` too. One shared helper that copies the guard plus its requires would mean the next sibling require breaks one place, loudly.
- The per-flag config tests (`zero-tool-done-guard-config` and others) each re-test the parse. Now they could just pin "this flag is envFlag, default X".
- Some reworded config.js comments wrap awkwardly.
- My commit message says "13 inline copies". It was 16 sites.

**4. If the area were how I'd want it, what would this ticket have been?** "Make SD_X default-on": a one-word diff plus a test. The helper should have appeared when the second boolean flag was written. Every "same idiom as X, copied verbatim" comment was a note that it hadn't.

**5. What did the ticket or plan get wrong?** Little on substance. The 16-site count, the rule, the `.env` hazard and the leaf requirement were all right. The gaps:
- It named `watch-restart.sh --check` as the reason to keep instance-guard standalone, but didn't follow that to the fixtures that simulate it. "Existing per-flag tests stay as they are" was true, yet four other tests needed a line each.
- It listed `npm run test:mutation` as a witness. That run needs `HARBOUR_DIR` and edits Harbour's source, so in this workspace it isn't a routine check.
- It expected `test:system` to be a clean signal, but main already fails 4 tests there.
